name: Waif
subcategory: A young person who is thin and looks unhealthy or uncared for
summary: This article is about the Coquette sub-aesthetic.
description:
This article is about the Coquette sub-aesthetic. For the anime "femcel" aesthetic, see Femcel .

Waif , also known as Girlblogger, Female Manipulator, or Femcel, is an internet aesthetic and persona within the Coquette sphere. It revolves around a modern archetype of a young woman who is intelligent, misunderstood, beautiful, and emotionally troubled, often exhibiting self-destructive, toxic, or manipulative tendencies. The imagery of the aesthetic reflects that complex lifestyle, emphasizing both its chaotic nature and its aspirational qualities.

The Waif aesthetic is one of many that developed out of the Heroin Chic trend and its cultural influence over womanhood. Waif draws significant inspiration from the Dark Nymphet, Sadgirl and pro-ana communities. Some of the defining features of this aesthetic are its relation to media about unlikable, flawed female protagonists and a cynical, detached sense of humor (partially inspired by the podcast Red Scare ). Waif content is not limited to curated images; it is also heavily conveyed through memes, mood boards, anonymous confessions on the app Whisper, and text posts about users' personal lives.

While it shares visuals with many Coquette-related aesthetics, its unique embrace of controversial values and viewpoints, unashamed portrayal of mental illness, and acceptance of toxic personality traits sets it apart.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Preoccupation with beauty and thinness, performative narcissism, intellectual pretension, embracing "unlikable" traits and female protagonists

visualDNA.colour: White, gray, black, pink, blue, beige

fashion.Overview: Waif fashion largely originates from the hyper-feminine luxury fashion of the 2000s McBling aesthetic, the original Dark Nymphet aesthetic, and trends of the early 2020s such as Coquette, Dollette and Balletcore. The styling can range from being prim and polished to messy and disorganized, tailored to the specific Waifs' persona. The through line that connects it all together is the emphasis on skinniness, which is seen as aspirational to those without it and as a status symbol for those with it. One way this is shown is through wearing Brandy Melville, a brand known for having "one-size-fits-all" clothing that only fits on thin, petite women. The garments that are based on 2000s trends,…
fashion.Tops: Camisoles and tanktops; Babydoll tops; Milkmaid-style blouses; Baby tees; Henley tops
fashion.Bottoms: Pleated mini skirts; Plaid and check mini skirts, often from Burberry and with the distinctive belt piece detail; Chiffon wrap skirts used in ballet practice clothing; Low-waisted jeans; Bootcut jeans; Denim Mini shorts; Straight leg sweatpants; Leggings, often black or gray, sometimes flared
fashion.Dresses: Slip dresses; Babydoll dresses; Mini dresses; A-line; Smocked, ruched; Short, puff sleeves; Lace trim
fashion.Outerwear: Fur coats; Winter coats with faux-fur trimmed hoods; Tight-fitting cardigans; Puffer jackets; Knit Cardigans; Tight hoodies; Peacoats
fashion.Shoes: UGG boots (Coquette slipper, Mini Bailey Bow, Mini Dipper Legwarmers, etc.); Leather patent heels; Fold-over boots; Ballet flats; Mary Janes; Ballet-inspired shoes (Puma Speedcat, Adidas Samba Janes, etc.); Strappy heels
fashion.Accessories: Sheer tights and stockings; Visible underwear such as whale tail thongs ( Red Scare sells some as merch), lace-trimmed panties and bralettes; Dainty jewelry; Pearls and pearl detailing; Vivienne Westwood jewelry, especially with the Orb logo pendant; Crosses, crucifixes, and rosaries; Leg-warmers; Totes and slouchy/hobo bags; Vintage purses; Fur hats; Bows, ribbons and headbands
fashion.Brands: Brandy Melville; Hollister; Aeropostale; Abercrombie and Fitch; Gilly Hicks; Victoria's Secret and Victoria Secret's PINK; Dior; NYX; Too faced; essence; Diptyque; Vivienne Westwood
